permits.name: Form your legal entity with the Illinois Secretary of State (LLC / corporation)
permits.issuing_agency: Illinois Secretary of State – Business Services
permits.notes: LLC Articles of Organization are $150 online with roughly 10 business days processing, or $250 for 24-hour expedited service; a name can be reserved for 90 days for $25. LLCs then file an annual report each year. Do this first: the EIN, IDOR registration, lease and every liquor application need the exact entity name. If you trade under a different name, file an assumed name with the Secretary of State (LLCs) or the county clerk (sole proprietors).

permits.name: Illinois Department of Revenue business registration (REG-1: sales tax + withholding)
permits.issuing_agency: Illinois Department of Revenue (IDOR) – MyTax Illinois
permits.notes: Register through MyTax Illinois ('Register a New Business (Form REG-1)') before you make purchases, sales or hire employees; online registrations take about one to two business days, paper filings four to six weeks. One registration covers Retailers' Occupation (sales) tax and employee withholding, and you can register with IDES for unemployment in the same session. Print the Certificate of Registration: Chicago BACP and the ILCC ask for your IDOR account number.

permits.name: IDES unemployment insurance employer registration
permits.notes: A newly created business must register with IDES within 30 days of start-up, online through MyTax Illinois (or on paper form REG-UI-1). You receive a seven-digit UI account number used for quarterly wage reports and contributions. Free; your payroll provider needs the number before the first pay run.

permits.name: Workers' compensation insurance
permits.issuing_agency: Any licensed carrier or the assigned-risk pool (regulated by the Illinois Workers' Compensation Commission)
permits.notes: Illinois requires virtually every employer to carry workers' compensation from the first employee, including part-time and family workers. Premiums are a percentage of payroll set by class code, not a fee. Operating without coverage exposes owners to stop-work orders and per-day fines from the IWCC insurance compliance unit, and Chicago license inspectors may ask for the certificate.

permits.name: Dram shop (liquor liability) insurance
permits.issuing_agency: Licensed insurance carrier (required by the Illinois Liquor Control Act)
permits.notes: Illinois retailers must carry dram shop liability coverage at the statutory limits, and both the local liquor commission and the ILCC require the certificate before a license is issued. Premiums depend on alcohol sales mix, hours and entertainment, and late-hour bars pay considerably more. Get quotes during lease negotiation so the cost is in your pro forma.

permits.name: Local liquor license from your city, village or county (required before the state license)
permits.issuing_agency: Local Liquor Control Commissioner (mayor / village president; county board chair in unincorporated areas)
permits.notes: Illinois licenses alcohol locally first: you must hold a local retail liquor license before the ILCC will issue a state license, and the state application asks for the local license number, issue and expiration dates. Every municipality sets its own classes, fees, quotas and hearing process, and some cap the number of licenses per class. In unincorporated areas the county is the local authority. Chicago applicants use the BACP Tavern or Consumption on Premises license instead.

permits.name: Illinois Liquor Control Commission state Retailer's liquor license
permits.issuing_agency: Illinois Liquor Control Commission (ILCC) – Liquor Control & Compliance Portal
permits.notes: Filed online through the ILCC Liquor Control & Compliance Portal (iLogin) after your local license is issued; attach the local license, IDOR registration and dram shop certificate. No alcohol may be sold before the state license date. The same retailer license covers beer, wine and spirits; local classes are what distinguish a tavern from a restaurant.
permits.stall_risk: Operators assume the state license can run in parallel with the local one; it cannot, so the state step adds 2–6 weeks after the local license is in hand. Have the ILCC portal account, dram shop certificate and IDOR number ready the day the local license is issued.

permits.name: BASSET alcohol seller/server certification
permits.issuing_agency: Illinois Liquor Control Commission – BASSET licensed trainers
permits.notes: Illinois requires everyone who serves, sells or checks IDs for alcohol at on-premises licensees, plus their managers, to complete BASSET training within 120 days of hire; certification is valid for three years. Cook County and Chicago have required it for years, and some municipalities also require it for bouncers. The on-premise course is about four hours, online or in person; verify cards with the ILCC BASSET Card Lookup.

permits.name: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM, formerly FSSMC) + allergen awareness training
permits.issuing_agency: ANSI-accredited exam provider (ServSafe, NRFSP, Prometric, 360training) per the Illinois Food Code / IDPH
permits.notes: In medium- and high-risk establishments every Person in Charge must hold an ANSI-accredited CFPM certificate, valid five years, and one must be on duty whenever food is prepared or served. CFPMs in Category I (high-risk) restaurants must also complete allergen awareness training within 30 days of hire and every three years. Chicago additionally requires a City of Chicago Food Service Sanitation Certificate, issued on the basis of the ANSI certificate.

permits.name: Food handler training (ANSI-accredited, all food employees)
permits.issuing_agency: ANSI-accredited food handler training provider (Illinois Food Handling Regulation Enforcement Act)
permits.notes: Food employees generally must complete food handler training within 30 days of hire and renew every three years; restaurant staff must use an ANSI-accredited program (IDPH only approves internal programs for non-restaurants). Employees who hold a CFPM certificate are exempt. Keep training records on site for the health inspector.

permits.name: Hotel Operators' Occupation Tax (HOOT) registration
permits.notes: Anyone renting sleeping rooms for fewer than 30 consecutive days must register for HOOT through MyTax Illinois and file monthly on Form RHM-1. The state rate works out to about 5.64% of gross rental receipts (6% tax on 94% of receipts); Chicago locations also owe the state-administered Municipal Hotel Tax, the MPEA tax and the Illinois Sports Facilities tax, plus the city's own Hotel Accommodations Tax filed with Chicago Finance.
